events.title: The martyrdom of St. John Ogilvie
events.shortBlurb: Scotland's only post-Reformation martyr was hanged at Glasgow Cross for refusing the king's supremacy over the Church…
body: Born about 1580 at Drumnakeith in Banffshire and raised a Calvinist, John Ogilvie was received into the Church at Louvain in 1597 and entered the Society of Jesus two years later. Ordained at Paris in 1613, he begged for the Scottish mission and returned home that November, disguised as a horse trader, to minister in secret about Glasgow.

His mission lasted less than a year. Arrested in October 1614, he was tortured by sleeplessness and pressed to own King James's supremacy in the Church, which he refused — he would acknowledge it, he said, no more than that of an old hat. Condemned for treason, he was hanged at Glasgow Cross on 10 March 1615, throwing his hidden rosary into the crowd as he died.

Out of open popular sympathy the customary quartering was spared him. Beatified in 1929, he was canonized by Paul VI on 17 October 1976 — the only post-Reformation martyr of Scotland raised to the altars.
